scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: In a crash, an airbag fills up faster than you can blink. How does a bag inflate that fast?

scenes.name: sensor
scenes.text: Sensors called accelerometers feel how fast the car is slowing down. A crash means a sudden, violent drop in speed.

scenes.name: decide
scenes.text: A control unit checks the signal, and decides within a few milliseconds whether the crash is serious enough.

scenes.name: ignite
scenes.text: If it is, it fires a tiny igniter, which starts a fast chemical reaction inside the inflator.

scenes.name: gas
scenes.text: The reaction releases a burst of gas, mostly nitrogen, which blasts the folded bag open in about thirty milliseconds.

scenes.name: deflate
scenes.text: The bag has small vents, so it starts to deflate as you hit it. That cushions you, instead of bouncing you back.

scenes.name: belt
scenes.text: Airbags are made to work with seatbelts. Without a belt, the bag itself can hurt you.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Sense, decide, ignite, inflate. Faster than a blink. Follow for more on how things really work.
